title: #16 D-098: every issuer round starts on its target's current head with only the ticket's own commits
objective: Before the agents of any issuer round start, t/<N> and t/<N>-cases consist of the current head of the ticket's target plus only that ticket's own commits whenever those commits replay cleanly, with the target sha each branch was put on recorded on the ticket.
outline: The replay rule (D-098): for each branch, S (start) and the own commits are: t/<N>-cases (when the branch exists): S = the target's current head T; own = `git rev-list --reverse --first-parent --no-merges t/<N>-cases --not X T`. t/<N>: S = the rebased t/<N>-cases head when the old t/<N> contained the old t/<N>-cases head (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`) and that replay succeeded, else T; own = `git rev-list --reverse --first-parent --no-merges t/<N> --not X T [old t/<N>-cases head]`. X = the ticket's branch_base[<branch>] when recorded, plus every branch that exists and that the ticket's history names as 'target' of an 'issuer started' event (claim() writes one for the current target before round 1). The first-parent walk skips merge commits and everything only reachable through their second parent (a step-6 merge of the target, the worker's merge of the cases branch or of the target); excluding the old targets also covers a branch made before this change (no branch_base: the request's 'merge-base with the old target' - `--not <old target>` excludes at least that) and a worker that put its branch linearly on a target. Consequence, written down on purpose: a ticket whose own commits already reached an earlier target (merged there, then its group was cancelled and the ticket readied) replays none of them and starts over on T - they are that group's unverified commits (D-098 3). With no branch_base and no history target only T is excluded (measured in the throwaway repo: then the commit the branch was made on leaks), which applies only to tickets with no 'issuer started' event left in their 50-event history. Where: devloop/ticket_issuer.py Issuer._round(), right after the existing `if need_cases:` branch_tree of the cases worktree and before `work = ... self.start("worker" ...)` - a new method (suggested name rebase_round(t, r)); go() is not changed (it already makes t<N> from the target when the branch is new). Steps: (a) self.owned(self.ticket()) first, as integrate() does, so an issuer that lost its ticket rewrites nothing; (b) a missing <worktrees>/t<N> is made again with the existing remake_tree(self.wt, self.branch) (#133); (c) in each worktree that will be replayed: run `merge|rebase|cherry-pick|revert --abort` (check=False, as auto_fixer.round_start does), then when Git.dirty() commit all tracked changes (`commit -a`) with author and committer devloop <devloop@localhost> set through GIT_AUTHOR_NAME, GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL, GIT_COMMITTER_NAME and GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL in the command's env (as Git.commit_files does - `-c user.name=...` loses to those variables, and the test harness sets them to 't') and subject 'devloop: uncommitted changes in <branch> at the start of round <r>'; the replay sets only GIT_COMMITTER_NAME/EMAIL to devloop (rebase keeps each commit's author); (d) t/<N>-cases first, then t/<N>, each replayed in place in the worktree that has it checked out (self.wt; self.cwt when it exists - need_cases has just made it); a t/<N>-cases with no worktree is replayed in a throwaway worktree on the branch itself made with self.repo.worktree(path, branch) (Git.worktree: no devloop.worktree_setup) under <worktrees>/rebase-t<N>-cases and removed with self.repo.remove_worktree afterwards; never call `git worktree` directly (worktree lock, project memory); (e) the replay itself: suggested helpers in devloop/core/gitx.py, e.g. Git.own_commits(tip, exclude) -> list (the rev-list above) and Git.replay(start, commits) -> (ok, why) run in a worktree: no commits -> `reset --hard start`; else `rebase -i --empty=drop --onto start start` with env GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR set to a command that copies a written todo of 'pick <sha>' lines (a temp file); on a non-zero exit collect why (CONFLICT lines, else the unmerged paths, else git's last line - the shape of Git.merge's why), `rebase --abort`, return (False, why); (f) one self.save() after both branches: branch_base[<branch>] = T's sha for every existing branch, and one event per branch whose head changed: event(t, 'rebased', branch=<branch>, onto=self.target, base=<T sha>, replayed=<number of commits replayed>); then use the saved ticket for the rest of the round. Item 8's interim: on any failure put both branches back (t/<N>-cases with Git.move_ref compare-and-swap from its new head to its old one and `reset --hard` in its worktree) and write nothing for them; the next ticket replaces this with the conflict round. Docs as in item 9; the docstring of ticket_issuer.py gets the step above '1. worker'. Nothing else reads branch_base; the group's own 'base' (main's sha when int/<g> was made) is a different fact and stays.

notes: Measured on 2026-11-24 on main 9f6cf16 (g10 landed) with the loop harness (opener scratch test kept at /home/user/agent-control-devloop/runs/creator/2026-11-24T140635Z-a1/repro/test_zz_d098_repro.py; copy it under tests_devloop/ of a scratch worktree and run it with run_tests.py to see today's behaviour): M1 retried ticket, same group: the round-1 worker started on t/1 without int/g1's head ('ancestor=no', own log 'work 1 old'). M2 moved ticket (t/1 made on int/g1 at 'work 5', took in int/g1 again after 'work 6', then put in g2): main got five.txt and six.txt. M6 the same with accepted cases on t/1-cases made in g1: main got five.txt and six.txt too; only r1-worker ran. M7 a dirty tracked file in <worktrees>/t1 at issuer start: the fake worker committed it inside its own 'work 1' commit (no devloop commit). M3 t/1 and int/g1 both change README.md (no verifier): the worker ran in all 6 rounds, every round a free 'merge' at step 6 ('merging the latest int/g1 into t/1 failed (CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in README.md) - another ticket of this group changed the same files; merge int/g1 yourself and resolve'), then stuck 'rounds'. M5 accepted cases on t/1-cases conflict (add/add cases/case_1.txt) with int/g1: the same 6 worker rounds, then stuck. M4 (request item 4, the fixer): main moved during the group's first full run; the regression went red and the controller started the fixer in the same step without follow_main (no 'main moved' group event before 'fix round 1'), but auto_fixer.fix() merged main into int/g1 before the fixer agent started (the agent's HEAD contained main, top commit "Merge branch 'main' into int/g1"; on a conflict the agent is told to merge it). So a fix round already starts from the latest main; no change is needed there. Git (2.43.0 here), measured in a throwaway repo: `git rebase --onto <new target> <base>` on a ticket branch that merged its old target replays the commits that merge brought in ('work 6' of another ticket reached the new group): dropping the merge commit is not enough, so the request's literal command is not used. `git rev-list --reverse --first-parent --no-merges <branch> --not <base> <old target> <new target> [<old cases head>]` lists exactly the ticket's own commits. `git rebase -i --empty=drop --onto S S` with GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR copying a written todo ('pick <sha>' lines) replays that list, drops a commit that became empty (rc 0), keeps the same shas when nothing changes, and on a conflict exits 1 with the unmerged paths in `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U`; `git rebase --abort` puts the branch back on its old head with a clean tree. An empty todo makes rebase -i exit 1 ('nothing to do'): with no own commits use `git reset --hard S` instead. cherry-pick on 2.43 stops on a commit that became empty (rc 1, 'now empty'), so it needs --skip handling if used. Design decisions: (1) the replay rule in the outline replaces the request's `git rebase --onto <target> <base>` because that command was measured to carry another group's commits; (2) branch_base is a new ticket field {branch: sha} written only by the issuer (it is state, like 'cases' and 'round'; `tickets.py ready`, `actl dag move` and revisions keep it); (3) uncommitted tracked changes are committed rather than dropped or stashed, so nothing a worker left is lost and the replay can run (a reset or rebase refuses or destroys a dirty tree); (4) the controller is not changed: the issuer always gets the current group's branch as --target, so every path that changes a ticket's group (actl dag move, a revise with a dag part, D-097's ungrouped ticket placed again, a ticket readied after stuck) is covered at the round start; (5) the fixer needs nothing (measured M4 above). Out of scope: rebasing int branches (they keep merging main); how a group lands; the worker and verifier prompts (the worker's 'merge the cases branch' step stays valid: after the replay t/<N> already contains the rebased cases branch when it held them); repairing branches in existing pools beyond what the round start does. Group g11 (the #16 group; g10 landed during this opening): this ticket touches ticket_issuer._round and core/gitx.py and adds one README paragraph between the DAG paragraph and the #74 paragraph; #134/#135 change ticket_controller.py, core/chain.py usage and the README groups paragraph, and #136 changes Issuer.stuck() - no shared function or paragraph, so no dependency.

request:
# New work starts from the latest verified point (docs/DECISIONS.md D-098; follow-up of GitHub issue #16)

The user's rule (2026-11-24, verbatim in D-098): 「反正我希望group 跑完驗證後 新的實作 都是基於那個點 ，後續的commit 都要先rebase 或是基於最新驗證過的點往後寫， 這是我的大原則」. Read D-097 and D-098 first, and the open tickets #134 #135 #136 (group g11), which change what happens to a stuck ticket's group; place this work so it does not conflict with them (core/chain.py; depend on them where it touches the same code). Tests go in the area's own test file in tests_devloop/ using loop_harness.py; each case runs in seconds.

What the main session read in the code (inference, not measured; measure it first and write what you find in the ticket):
- devloop/core/gitx.py `Git.worktree(path, branch, start)`: when the branch t/N already exists it is checked out as it is; `start` is used only for a new branch. devloop/ticket_issuer.py `go()` calls it with start=target once, then runs rounds; the ticket branch takes in the target only at the end of a round (step 6, "take in the latest target ... move the target").
- So a retried ticket (stuck, then readied) and a ticket moved to another group (`actl dag move`, `actl new --revise` with a dag part, D-097's ungrouped ticket later placed) keep the base they were made from. A worker writes on an old base, and for a moved ticket the old group's commits that were never verified come along when it merges into its new group (T: #320's branch was made from g63's int branch, then #320 was put in g88).

Wanted:
1. Before every round's agent starts (worker, and the verifier's cases branch where it has one), the ticket branch is rebased onto the current head of its target (the group's int branch, which already takes main when a group lands: ticket_controller.py follow_main). Only the ticket's own commits are replayed: the commits on t/N (and t/N-cases) that are not on the base it was last put on. Record that base on the ticket (e.g. `base` sha written when the branch is made or rebased) so a later rebase can use `git rebase --onto <target> <base>`; for a branch made before this change with no recorded base, use the merge-base with the branch's old target if it is known, else with the new target.
2. A ticket that changes group (any path) or comes back to ready after stuck: at its next round its branch is rebased onto the new target with only its own commits (as 1); commits of the old group that are not on the new target never reach it. If the ticket's own commits include merges of its old target (step 6 of an earlier round), those merges are not replayed.
3. A rebase with conflicts is aborted and handled like today's merge conflict when taking in the target: the worker gets the conflict to resolve on a branch that starts from the new target, and the round counts as a conflict round (free, as today). Never force anything onto the target or main; only t/N and t/N-cases are rewritten (they are devloop's own branches, nobody else's checkout).
4. The fixer (auto_fixer on a group's int branch) already works on the group's branch after follow_main; check that a fix round starts only after the group's branch has taken in the latest main (follow_main ran for that main sha), and say in the ticket whether that already holds.
5. Document in devloop/README.md: "every round starts from the latest verified point" with what is rebased, when, and what happens on conflict.
- removes: work on a stale base; a moved ticket carrying another group's unverified commits.
- Out of scope: rebasing int branches (they keep merging main; they are shared by the group's tickets); changing how a group lands.
